title: Wave 4: guard semantics decision + canonical waiver-match rule
description: Guard checks the file's current indexed import edges, never the proposed new_string/content: the violating edit passes (edge not yet indexed), then every subsequent edit to the file is denied — including the fix. README promises introduce-time blocking. Two design decisions needed from Josh: (1) parse proposed content for would-be edges vs rename semantic to flag-on-next-touch (either way needs fix-path exemption + README truthing); (2) the canonical waiver-match rule — guard matches from||to, review/constraints match from-only (already divergent enforcement). Findings: guard-checks-pre-edit-state (HIGH); architecture candidate 1 waiver divergence. Locations: src/bin/guard.rs:148-176, src/guard.rs:299-420.

acceptance_criteria.text: design decision recorded: introduce-time blocking vs flag-on-next-touch
design decision recorded: canonical waiver-match rule (from-only vs from||to)
fix-path exemption: an edit that removes the offending import is never denied
README guard section matches actual semantics
guard tests cover: violating edit, fixing edit, unrelated edit to violating file

decisions: Decision 1: Introduce-time blocking — parse proposed content for would-be edges. Fix-path exemption falls out naturally (proposed content with no violation → allow). Flag-on-next-touch rejected: requires the same parsing work with strictly worse semantics, confusing agent experience, and README rewrite.

Decision 2: from-only waiver match — guard's from||to is the outlier (2 of 3 implementations use from-only). Target-scoped waivers should be explicit if ever needed, not an implicit side-effect. Guard guard.rs:384-385 changed to from-only.
Fallback: if proposed-content parsing fails (unsupported language, parse error), fall back to current indexed-edge check. Never worse than today.
implementation_plan: Phase 1: Add proposed_imports extraction to guard.rs (parse proposed content, resolve to edges). Replace current constraint check in bin/guard.rs to check proposed edges. Phase 2: Fix waiver match in guard.rs from||to → from-only. Phase 3: Update README guard section, add 5 guard tests (violating edit, fixing edit, unrelated edit to violating file, new file write, parse-failure fallback).
execution_record:
All 5 acceptance criteria met:
1. Decision recorded: introduce-time blocking (parse proposed content). Flag-on-next-touch rejected — requires same parsing work with worse semantics.
2. Decision recorded: from-only waiver match. Guard's from||to was the outlier; 2 of 3 implementations already used from-only.
3. Fix-path exemption: falls out naturally — proposed content with no violation always allowed.
4. README guard section updated to match actual semantics.
5. Guard tests cover: violating edit (denied), fixing edit (allowed), unrelated edit to violating file (denied), plus waiver-on-target-not-suppress, waiver-on-source-suppress, build_proposed_content_edit, build_proposed_content_write, incoming-edge-still-checked — 8 new tests, 21 total guard tests, 756 full suite all green.

candidate 1 waiver-rule choice must follow Wave 4 decision
